analyst_view.overall: Club Brugge (9th) and Liverpool (8th) are level on 9 points, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Both arrive in form: Brugge won 5-1 at Mechelen on Saturday with two goals from Nicolo Tresoldi, who is over his concussion, and Freddie Potts and Jorne Spileers played the full game; Jan Virgili (counted by the numbers) is still out. Liverpool thrashed ten-man Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday under Andoni Iraola, with Virgil van Dijk fit and Gravenberch and Frimpong back, while Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are not yet selectable and Hugo Ekitike (counted) is still out with his Achilles injury. The numbers already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting, and no referee has been named yet. I found nothing they can't see, so I stay with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, already up a little for both attacks' form and down about 3% for Virgili's absence. Brugge scored five on Saturday and Liverpool four on Sunday, but that kind of form is exactly what the numbers' recent-games adjustment counts. Ekitike has been out for months, so I stay at 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.2 corners, 6 of them Liverpool's, and already add about 3% for Liverpool's high corner count lately. Frimpong is back on the right, so Liverpool's wide play should look like it has recently. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.1 cards and already add about 6% for Brugge's recent cards and take a little off Liverpool's. The referee is not named yet and there is no rivalry between the clubs. I stay at about 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.4 shots and have already pushed both sides up by 15-17% for their recent shooting. Liverpool's 4-0 against ten men and Brugge's 5-1 at Mechelen fit that picture rather than add to it, so I see no reason to go further and stay at 34.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target, already up for Brugge's sharp finishing (+8%) and Liverpool's volume (+5%). Both attacks are near full strength, with Tresoldi scoring again and Ekitike's long absence already in Liverpool's form, so I stay at 11.5.
